title: Chart assemble requirements, RapidChart opening view
subtitle: Demographics, allergies, meds, last 5 encounters, problems; 1.8s p95; partial fill with banners
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Rahul Deshmukh (PM), RapidChart consumers, backend, QA, Denise Howell (nursing informatics)
owners: Aman Kumar (PRD), Kavya Menon (assemble handler), Rahul Deshmukh (scope)
summary: Product requirements for GET /v1/chart/assemble, the opening chart RapidChart paints for a nurse on a unit. One payload: demographics, allergies, medications, last five encounters, problems. p95 1.8s at the API. If ChartLine, SiteNotes, or a facility feed is down, we still return 200 with partial blocks and banners. We do not pretend missing allergies are 'no known allergies.' Users are RapidChart nurses (ED, med-surg, and the other floors that already live in that app), not a future FHIR client. Success is time to first allergy view and honest banners, not assemble request counts. Notes text search is out of scope.
form_description: PRD for Riverview chart assemble: blocks, latency budget, partial-fill banners, caching, and success metrics tied to nurse time rather than QPS.
revision_history: Draft after Gita Raman's consume list and Denise's banner comments
Scope lock: five blocks, no notes search
Cache TTLs and SiteNotes Friday behavior
1.8s p95, metrics, open questions for nursing session still unscheduled

blocks.text: Problem

RapidChart currently fans out to ChartLine and SiteNotes on its own, with a 3.6s p95 opening view on RVH-MAIN weekdays (Gita Raman's Jan 28 numbers, n=8.2k views). Nurses wait, then see a layout that can paint meds before allergies, then sometimes see an empty allergy list when ChartLine timed out. Denise Howell called that empty list 'the dangerous quiet.' Northstar already decided the protocol is custom REST, not FHIR (RVH-TDD-2020-011). This PRD is the assemble product: what blocks, how fast, what happens when a source is down, how we cache, how we know we succeeded.

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: Ship GET /v1/chart/assemble as the only opening-view call RapidChart needs. Five blocks: demographics, allergies, meds, last 5 encounters, problems. API p95 1.8s. Partial fill + banners if a source fails. SiteNotes failure must not hide allergies. Success metric is nurse time to first allergy view on RapidChart (TFA), plus banner correctness, not QPS. Out of scope: notes full text, notes search, FHIR, cross-facility fuzzy name search.

Anita Shah backed the banner rule in a Feb 9 email: empty allergy block on timeout is a clinical assertion we did not mean to make. Rahul locked notes search out after Priya priced a SiteNotes index job at $14.6k extra vendor work this quarter, which we do not have. Luis Ortega's LDAP path authenticates the caller; it does not belong in the assemble JSON. Sneha Iyer tests this PRD. Diego Alvarez is not on the account yet.
Who the users are

Primary user: a Riverview nurse using RapidChart on a unit workstation, 11 facilities. Denise is the informatics owner. Charge-nurse voices we already have: Marisol Vega (ED, MAIN) and Patrice Coleman (med-surg, WEST). They do not log into patient-api. They should not hear about namespaces or FHIR. Secondary user: RapidChart application engineers (Gita) who must consume one JSON document. Tertiary: CensusBoard may not use assemble; they keep /v1/census/status. Do not force Omar Haddad onto this payload.
Not users: payers, HIEs, researchers, the CMIO looking at population dashboards. Chris Patel may sample anonymized timings. He does not get chart bodies in a warehouse from this project.

blocks.text: Scope
In

items: GET /v1/chart/assemble for one patient at one facility (facility code required).
Blocks: demographics, allergies, meds, encounters (exactly last 5 by start time desc), problems.
partial: boolean, banners: array of typed codes RapidChart already knows how to theme.
source_ts per upstream so RapidChart can show 'allergies as of 14:02' if they want. They asked for the timestamps; we will send them.
Cache assembled payloads in Redis (see caching).
Circuit and feed-disable behavior will be documented in a runbook; this PRD requires that a disabled feed still 200s with banners, never 503 the whole API.
Auth: caller must pass LDAP-backed bearer as the rest of patient-api. Unauthenticated assemble is out (privacy).

blocks.text: Out

items: Notes body and notes search. SiteNotes remains a later block or a separate call if RapidChart still wants a tab. Friday flakiness is exactly why notes are not on the opening critical path.
FHIR Bundles, $everything, contained resources (RVH-TDD-2020-011).
Writing back to ChartLine (meds rec, allergy add).
Cross-facility search and identity merge UX (RVH-TDD-2021-004 is a different design).
Pretty demographic formatting (name case, ZIP+4). Gita can format. We send what ChartLine sends, trimmed. If nursing later marks this P0, reopen; as of Feb 18 it is noise.
CensusBoard discharge lag. Different endpoint. Do not hide that work inside assemble.
Patient photos, insurance cards, PDF reprints.

blocks.text: Rejected alternative: a 'full chart' assemble that includes notes text 'because the nurse might need it.' Kavya measured SiteNotes p95 at 2.4s on Friday Jan 29, 16:10-17:40 Eastern, and 410ms on Tuesday morning. Putting notes on the critical path makes the 1.8s budget a joke on the day they most want the rest of the chart. Denise agreed notes can spinner on a second tab. Do not sneak notes into blocks in a hotfix.
Functional requirements
R1 Blocks and emptiness

Each block is either filled, empty-because-none, or missing-because-source. RapidChart must be able to tell those apart. empty-because-none is allowed to render 'no known allergies' only when ChartLine returned a successful empty list. missing-because-source must render a banner and must not use the 'no known' string. This is the load-bearing requirement. Anita and Denise both signed it in email (thread 2021-02-09).

rows: Missing-source: banner chartline_unavailable, do not invent a name
Empty-none only on HTTP 200 empty from ChartLine allergy query
If ADT fails, missing-source, do not reuse stale 5 from another patient
May collapse UI but banner stays
blocks.caption: Block/source matrix. Mixing patients in cache is a Sev-1, not a cosmetic bug.

blocks.text: R2 Partial fill

If ChartLine allergy query fails and meds succeed, HTTP 200, partial=true, banners includes allergy_unavailable (or chartline_unavailable if the whole interface is dead), meds filled, allergies missing-source. If SiteNotes is down, assemble does not care in v1 because notes are out. If we add a stub field notes_status later, it can be skipped without failing the opening view. Friday SiteNotes outages (observed 16:00-18:30 Eastern, 7 of last 8 Fridays in Jan-Feb) must not 5xx assemble.

If all ChartLine queries fail, still 200 when the circuit is open, all clinical blocks missing-source, banners chartline_unavailable. When circuit is closed, 502/504 is allowed so RapidChart can retry at their layer. Default in prod should move toward open-circuit + banners once the runbook exists; until then Kavya will ship closed and we will eat 5xx during ChartLine deaths. Rahul accepts that as a known gap (OQ-3).
R3 Last 5 encounters

Last 5 by encounter start descending at that facility. Not last 5 across the network. Cross-facility encounter mashup is an identity-merge problem. If fewer than 5 exist, return what exists, not padded nulls. Do not include cancelled encounters ChartLine marks canceled=true.
R4 Facility required

facility query param required, enum of 11 codes (RVH-MAIN, RVH-WEST, RVH-EAST, RVH-NORTH, RVH-SOUTH, RVH-PEDS, RVH-REHAB, RVH-BH, RVH-ASC, RVH-CLINIC-07, RVH-CLINIC-12). Unknown code: 400 bad_facility. Missing code: 400. We do not guess MAIN.
R5 Identity

patient_id is our merge key, not MRN in the URL. RapidChart may hold MRN internally; they hash or map before calling us, or they call a patient lookup we already have. Logs must not print MRN (a later SOP will spell this out; for this PRD: assemble logs facility + mrn_hash + trace_id). RVH-BH: same assemble, same blocks, tighter auth group. No extra fields.
Latency budget

API p95 1.8s for HTTP 200 assemble, measured at ingress, weekday 07:00-19:00 Eastern, RVH-MAIN+WEST combined, excluding feed-disabled facilities. p99 3.2s. Not a marketing SLO; Priya will put 99.5% non-5xx on the ops page separately. The 1.8s number is what Gita said RapidChart can add 200-400ms of paint to and still beat their current 3.6s p95 opening view. If we come in at 1.9s we did not meet this PRD.

May be one vendor call; if two, still parallel
blocks.caption: Budget sketch. Parallel ChartLine calls are mandatory. Serializing them will miss 1.8s.

blocks.text: Timeouts: per ChartLine subcall 700ms. If allergies time out at 700ms, do not wait for a slow problems call to finish the whole handler if problems already returned. Handler budget 1.6s internally so ingress 1.8s has room. SiteNotes is not on this path.
Caching

Redis key chart:v1:{facility}:{mrn_hash}. TTL 120s on a full success (partial=false). TTL 25s on partial=true so we do not glue a ChartLine outage into a two-minute lie. Do not cache 4xx. Do not cache 5xx. Cache key must include facility so MAIN and WEST never share a body. Cache value is the exact JSON RapidChart gets, minus Authorization.

Rejected alternative: 15 min TTL 'because ChartLine is expensive.' Kavya ran the math: 15 min would have served the Jan 12 allergy dictionary delay as truth to WEST med-surg. Denise would like us not to. 120s is the compromise with ChartLine's 12.4 QPS cap on our service account (Mei Chen's email Feb 3). If we miss-storm, we will be the people who knocked ChartLine over. HPA and cache exist so we do not.

Stampede: single-flight per key in-process, plus Redis SET NX lock 2s for cross-pod. If lock fails, wait 50ms and GET again, up to 4 times, then fetch anyway. Documented so on-call does not disable the lock during a 5xx hunt.

blocks.text: Priya's steering one-pager: we are buying nurse time and honest emptiness, not a unified platform story. Request counts will go down if RapidChart stops fanout retries, which is good. If they go up, look for retries and ChartLine 504s, not 'adoption.' Aman owns this PRD file. Kavya owns the handler. Rahul owns saying no to notes search when it comes back the week after demo.
Failure modes and how RapidChart should behave

This is the section a VP can skip and an engineer cannot. Assemble will fail in pieces. RapidChart 4.3.x still has code paths that treat HTTP 200 as 'all blocks trustworthy' and HTTP 5xx as a full-screen error. Both are wrong for this PRD.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: HTTP 200 with partial=true is a clinical warning, not a success you can cache in the workstation for the rest of the shift. RapidChart must not write a partial allergy block into its local session store as 'no known allergies.' Gita has a ticket RCHART-884 for that store. If it is not fixed before they flip the feature flag, we do not flip.

Worked example, ChartLine allergy 504, everything else 200, circuit still closed on other subcalls that succeeded. Handler waits 700ms on allergies, marks missing-source, returns 200 in ~740ms if cache miss on the other blocks already in flight.

blocks.caption: Partial fill contract. null vs [] is load-bearing.

blocks.text: If RapidChart cannot distinguish null from [], we have not met R1 even if our OpenAPI is pretty. Sneha's suite must decode with a parser that keeps null. Luis will not special-case LDAP for this; 401/403 remain empty bodies with no blocks, not partial charts. A 403 that includes demographics would be a privacy incident.
Timeouts, retries, and the 12.4 QPS cap

Two retries at 80ms backoff on a 700ms timeout is how you turn one ChartLine blip into three calls and a 2.1s handler. Cap retries at 2 total attempts (1 retry) per subcall, and skip retry when the error is 401 from ChartLine (our client cert) or 400 (our bug). Retry 504 and TCP reset only. If all four ChartLine subcalls retry, we can 8x a miss storm. Single-flight is per assemble key, not per subcall; subcalls still parallel inside one flight.

Mei Chen's 12.4 QPS cap is per service account, all facilities. MAIN 07:30-09:00 is 6.8 QPS historical from RapidChart's own fanout (Jan). If we cold-cache a rolling restart of 6 pods at 08:10 we will spike. Roll pods 1 at a time, 40s between, weekday restarts after 10:30 Eastern unless Sev-1. Kavya will put that in the deploy notes. This PRD makes it a requirement, not a courtesy.
What a wrong cache looks like

Symptom: nurse on WEST sees MAIN allergies. Cause: cache key omitted facility, or RapidChart posted the wrong facility code, or a hash collision (should be sha256 truncated, not 8 hex). Detection: Sneha's two-facility test, plus a prod metric assemble_cache_key_parts=3. If the metric ever shows 2, page. Recovery: DEL is not a global flush; see future runbook. Product requirement here: key shape is part of the PRD, not an impl detail Kavya can shorten.

blocks.text: Data quality we will not clean in assemble

ChartLine free-text doses, mixed-case names, ZIP without ZIP+4, hyphenated streets: pass through. Pretty print is out of scope (later P2 noise). If we start title-casing names we will break BH preferred names and peds guardians. Do not add a formatter because an executive screenshot looks messy.

Allergy codes: we send ChartLine's local code plus text. We do not translate to SNOMED in v1. A FHIR mapping layer might, later, if a contract says so. Putting SNOMED into RapidChart now without a terminology owner is how we print the wrong allergen.

Encounter types: EncTypeCd as ChartLine sends it, plus a display string if they send one. We do not invent 'Inpatient' vs 'ED' from bed numbers. Marisol will complain if ED shows as 'OBS' because ChartLine said OBS. That complaint belongs on Nate's interface queue, not as a silent remap in our handler.
Dependencies and non-goals recap

items: Depends on ChartLine iface and LDAP. Depends on Redis for the SLO, not for correctness; origin fetch must still be right if Redis is empty.
Depends on RapidChart consume (RCHART-884 and mount order). We can ship API on time and still fail TFA if they ignore the contract.
Does not depend on FHIR, HAPI, notes search, CensusBoard poll interval, or Diego's future SRE work.
Does not replace RVH-PRD-2020-019 (broader unified API). This PRD is the opening view slice. Broader CRUD stays on the older doc.
Will be cited by the later on-call runbook for banners and circuit. If the runbook disagrees on circuit default, runbook wins at 3am, this PRD gets a revision in daylight.
